criteria.text: Prior authorization is for use of more than one atypical antipsychotic (any age) or use of any atypical antipsychotic in a child less than 5 years of age.
Documentation of the condition being treated and that the addition of a second atypical antipsychotic is medically necessary (or, for age <5, that atypical therapy is medically necessary).
Documentation that the initial atypical antipsychotic cannot be discontinued with the addition of the second atypical antipsychotic.
A treatment plan that includes monitoring for adverse drug reactions, metabolic side effects, and efficacy.
Medication profile history showing at least 2 weeks of single-drug therapy at an adequate dose of the medication and progress notes.

notes: Partial encoding of Alaska Medicaid Atypical Antipsychotic Therapeutic Duplication Criteria Version 1; Last updated 4/25/2012; Approved 3/16/2012. Stub effective_date 1970-01-01 replaced with approval date 2012-03-16.
Applies to Abilify, Clozaril, Fanapt, Geodon, Invega, Latuda, Risperdal, Saphris, Seroquel, Seroquel XR, Symbyax, Zyprexa (oral and injectable).

PA trigger is closed: more than one atypical at any age, or any atypical in a child <5 years. Documentation bullets for dual therapy include inability to discontinue the initial agent and ≥2 weeks single-drug adequate-dose history; those two gates are when-gated to the therapeutic-duplication trigger only.

Length of approval (notes only): initial up to 3 months; renewals up to 1 year after the initial 3 months with documentation of ADR/metabolic monitoring and improved efficacy of combination therapy. Duration/renewal remain manual review.
